conclusionVerdicts.question: On engine 1.2.0, is a compound TTL index rejected, and with what error?
conclusionVerdicts.reason: Rerun step 15 returned the same reply byte for byte (code 67 CannotCreateIndex, same errmsg, no errorLabels key), and step 17 likewise for expireAfterSeconds 'abc'. The 0.117 report has the same code, codeName and rule text; its full errmsg differs only in the order of the echoed spec, because that run built the spec with create_index. The answer reports the real code and text (CannotCreateIndex, not 'unsupported') and is scoped to documentdb-local.

conclusionVerdicts.question: Can one collection carry a second single-field TTL index, and does that index expire documents on its own?
conclusionVerdicts.reason: Rerun: exp2_ttl accepted (numIndexesAfter 3); exp2_past_only and exp_future_exp2_past were purged by the first pg_cron run after the index existed (2026-11-25T21:23:00.016280Z, lag 21.0 s), and exp2_future_control survived 4 runs. The build-time sentence compares 2006 ms 'on the 10-document collection' with about 17 ms 'on the empty collection', which implies the documents cause the delay. They do not: in the supplementary probe, createIndexes on an existing but empty collection took 1004.8 ms (pexp_ttl_pfe) and 2007.5 ms (plain_idx). Only the createIndexes that also creates the collection returns in milliseconds (4.5 to 17.5 ms). Every slow call had one documentdb_index_build_task_1 run of 12.0 to 23.3 ms inside its window (idle runs take 1.5 to 2.9 ms). That indicates the index on an existing collection is built by the 2-second pg_cron index-build job, and the call returns about 1 or 2 s after it starts (an inference from cron.job_run_details).

conclusionVerdicts.question: Which values of a TTL-indexed field expire (Date, string, number, null, missing, array)?
conclusionVerdicts.reason: Rerun: past_date_60s and array_of_dates were purged; string_value, number_value (64-bit integer), null_value and missing_field survived 4 TTL runs. The tester observed only one numeric type (int64), so 'only BSON Dates' was a generalisation. The supplementary probe supports it: int32 epoch seconds, double and Decimal128 epoch ms, a BSON Timestamp, an ObjectId with a past embedded time, an embedded document holding a past Date, an empty array and a future-only array all survived 2 TTL runs. A past Date and the reversed-order array [Date +1 day, Date -60 s] were purged by the first run.

conclusionVerdicts.question: What is the TTL purge cadence and lag on engine 1.2.0 with open-source defaults?
conclusionVerdicts.reason: Rerun: the same pg_cron job and schedule. 6 runs, each starting 14 to 28 ms after a whole minute and lasting 2.3 to 8.6 ms, all succeeded. All 7 expired documents went at the first run after they became eligible, with 0 skipped runs. Lags were 21.0 to 50.9 s, against 22.0 to 57.0 s for the tester. This rerun inserted at hh:mm:37, while both tester runs were held to hh:mm:03, which directly confirms that the lag is the time to the next whole minute. The general expectation '0 to about 60 s plus milliseconds' is shown only when each run finishes its work in milliseconds (13 documents or fewer here). A backlog that needs the 1000-row batches or the 60 s budget was not tested.

conclusionVerdicts.question: Did TTL behaviour change between engine 0.117 and engine 1.2.0?
conclusionVerdicts.reason: The rerun matches the tester on every compared item. The 0.117 report shows the same errors, the same listIndexes entry for exp_ttl, the same survivors and a per-minute cadence. The settings remarks are source readings. On 1.2.0 the TTL-specific GUC has no visible effect: a plain non-TTL index (plain_idx) also got bson_extended_rum_composite_path_ops and storageEngine {enableOrderedIndex: true}. Neither the op class nor that listIndexes flag marks an index as TTL on this build.

conclusionVerdicts.question: Does the spec's command docker exec ddb-engine-test psql -U postgres -p 9712 -tAc "select jobname, schedule, command from cron.job" work on 1.2.0?
conclusionVerdicts.reason: Rerun step 03 exits 2 with the same 'role "postgres" does not exist'. The fallback lists the same 4 jobs, identical before and after. The tester recorded no step for 'PostgreSQL runs as OS user documentdb' or 'documentdb is the superuser and owns the pg_cron jobs'. The extra read-only checks E01 to E04 now back both: documentdb is the only superuser, no role is named postgres, all four cron.job rows have username documentdb, and the postmaster runs as OS user documentdb (uid 1000).

conclusionVerdicts.question: Does this settle the managed service's TTL purge cadence (DECISIONS topic 10, open item 5)?
conclusionVerdicts.reason: The answer correctly says no and stays inconclusive. The GUC values match the rerun's pg_settings exactly. The loop description matches ttl_index.c in the scratchpad engine-src copy, which is the main branch, not the 1.2.0 tag: the loop runs while elapsed time is within TTLTaskMaxRunTimeInMS (with repeatPurgeIndexesForTTLTask on) and stops when a pass deletes 0 rows. The engine logs 'TTL Index delete rows exceeded time budget' when a run passes its budget. No such line was among the last 30 matching log lines (step 23, about the last 28 minutes), which is consistent with no run reaching its budget.

conclusionVerdicts.question: Incidental: what shape do the gateway's createIndexes and drop replies have on 1.2.0?
conclusionVerdicts.reason: Rerun replies are identical: raw.defaultShard wrapper, hello msg 'isdbgrid', and {ok: 1.0, dropped: 'docs'} for dropping a collection that did not exist. The advice that a kit helper 'should look under raw.<shard>' goes past the evidence. Only the documentdb-local gateway was observed, and the kit targets the managed service, so a helper should accept both top-level counts and raw.<shard>. Also, 'as on 0.117' holds only for the reply shape. The 0.117 report reads 'dropped (or did not exist)', so it does not show that the 0.117 collection was absent.

extraObservations: The rerun inserted at hh:mm:37, while both tester runs were held to hh:mm:03. The already-expired documents waited 21 to 23 s instead of 55 to 57 s, and future_date_90s waited 48.0 s instead of 22.0 s. Purge time depends only on the phase of the next whole-minute pg_cron run.

A partialFilterExpression on a TTL index limits what the purger deletes, observed on 1.2.0. pexp_ttl_pfe {pexp: 1}, expireAfterSeconds 5, partialFilterExpression {purge: {$eq: true}} purged pfe_match. pfe_nomatch (purge false) and pfe_flag_missing (no purge field) survived 2 TTL runs. The PostgreSQL index carries WHERE (document #= '{ "purge" : true }'::bsonquery). Until now DECISIONS topic 10 had this only from a ttl_index.c comment.

Non-Date TTL values beyond the tester's set survived 2 TTL runs (2026-11-25T21:28:00.018699Z and 21:29:00.013006Z): int32, double, Decimal128, BSON Timestamp, ObjectId, embedded document {at: Date}, empty array, and array of future Dates. A [future, past] array was purged, so element order does not matter.

TTL index op class on 1.2.0: exp_ttl, exp2_ttl, pexp_ttl_pfe, frac_ttl and a plain non-TTL index all use documentdb_extended_rum with bson_extended_rum_composite_path_ops (pathspec single path, tl 2691). All non-_id indexes list storageEngine {enableOrderedIndex: true}. createTTLIndexAsCompositeByDefault is therefore not distinguishable on this build, and that listIndexes flag does not identify TTL indexes.

Index build path: createIndexes that auto-creates the collection returns in 4.5 to 17.5 ms. Any later createIndexes on that collection, empty or not, takes 1005 to 2010 ms, in about 1 s steps. Each such call had one documentdb_index_build_task_1 run of 12.0 to 23.3 ms inside its window, which indicates the build is done by the 2-second pg_cron index-build job and the call waits for it (an inference from cron.job_run_details).

TTL createIndexes validation codes on 1.2.0 vary by rule: negative expireAfterSeconds gives code 67 CannotCreateIndex ('cannot be less than 0'), and 2147483648 gives code 67 ('must be within an acceptable range'). TTL on _id gives code 197 InvalidIndexSpecificationOption. TTL on a hashed key gives code 115 CommandNotSupported ('Creating a hash index as ttl index is not supported.', with no 'Error in specification' prefix). expireAfterSeconds 5.7 is accepted and stored as 5 (truncated). None carried errorLabels.

collMod {collMod: 'supp', index: {name: 'exp_ttl', expireAfterSeconds: 7}} succeeds with reply {ok: 1, expireAfterSeconds_old: 5, expireAfterSeconds_new: 7.0} (new value echoed as a double), and listIndexes then shows 7.

When t_ttl_rerun got its first collection, the engine also created a system.dbSentinel collection (catalog rows 306 and 315, one per run). That is the source of the 'database ... has collections: false / Creating ... for the sentinel database' lines that the tester's step 23 counted as 'mention database t_ttl'. With documentdb.logTTLProgressActivity off (default), the engine logged no TTL progress lines, so the log cross-check cannot attribute purges. Only cron.job_run_details plus polling can.

documentdb.enable_ttl_cleanup_background is not an alternative purge path on main: delete_expired_rows_background in ttl_index.c returns immediately whether the setting is on or off. This is a main-branch source reading, not the 1.2.0 tag.

verdict.summary: Reproduced. The renamed copy (database t_ttl_rerun, no logic change) ran 26 steps in 242.4 s. Every compared step matched the tester's run 2: errors byte for byte, the same purged set and survivors, all purges at the first pg_cron run after eligibility. Lags were 21.0 to 50.9 s instead of 22.0 to 57.0 s because the insert was at hh:mm:37 instead of hh:mm:03. Three wording issues: the C2 build-time framing (the delay comes from the collection already existing, not from its documents), C4's general 0 to 60 s expectation (shown only for tiny backlogs), and C8's kit-helper advice (local gateway shape only). Evidence is about open-source engine and gateway 1.2.0 on documentdb-local, not the managed service.
